blocks.task_summary: Use Euler's method with step 0.03 to approximate y at x=0.15 for dy/dx=(x²-y²)/(x²+1) with y(0)=3, answer to 6 sf.
method_path: Iterate through x=0.03,0.06,0.09,0.12,0.15 to get y₅≈2.58046

evidence.basis: M1 attempt Euler's method; A1 y₁=2.91; A1 at least one correct intermediate to 3+ sf; A1 2.58046 [4 marks]

blocks.task_summary: (i) Write dy/dx at x=0 by substituting into DE. (ii) Show d²y/dx²=3 at x=0 by implicit differentiation using quotient/product rules.
method_path: Differentiate DE implicitly using quotient rule on (x²-y²)/(x²+1)
Apply product rule to d/dx(2xy) implicitly
accepted_alternatives: Rearrange DE to (x²+1)dy/dx=x²-y² then differentiate both sides using product rule and implicit differentiation

evidence.basis: (i) dy/dx=-3 A1; (ii) METHOD 1: quotient rule M1, product & implicit diff M1, deriv expression A1, d²y/dx²=3 AG A1. METHOD 2: rearrange then differentiate, A1 for LHS/RHS, M1 product & implicit. [5 marks]

blocks.task_summary: (i) Given d³y/dx³=9 at x=0, find first four terms of Maclaurin series for y. (ii) Use series to approximate y(0.15) to 6 sf.

evidence.basis: Maclaurin series 3-3x+(3/2)x²+(3/2)x³ A1A1 (A1 first three terms, A1 fourth term); y(0.15)=2.58881 A1 [3 marks]

blocks.task_summary: (i) Solve DE using partial fraction (1-x²)/(1+x²)≡2/(1+x²)-1, with y(0)=3, giving y=f(x). (ii) Evaluate y(0.15) to 6 sf.
accepted_alternatives: Integrating factor method: rewrite DE as dy/dx+(2x/(x²+1))y=0, IF=e^{∫2x/(x²+1)dx}=e^{-x+2arctan x}, then d/dx(e^{-x+2arctan x}y)=0, solve to y=3e^{2arctan x-x}

evidence.basis: EITHER separation of variables M1, ln y=2arctan x-x+c A1A1; OR integrating factor M1, IF=e^{-x+2arctan x} A1, e^{-x+2arctan x}y=A A1. M1 find c or A using (0,3); A1 c=ln3 or A=3; A1 y=3e^{2arctan x-x}. (ii) y(0.15)=2.58786 A1. [7 marks]

blocks.task_summary: For 0≤x<1, explain why Euler's method always gives an underestimate for y.
method_path: Note d²y/dx²>0 for 0≤x<1 (graph is concave up)
Euler's method uses tangent lines which lie below a concave up curve
Conclude the approximation is an underestimate

evidence.basis: graph of y=f(x) is concave up OR d²y/dx²>0 for 0≤x<1 A1; hence tangents used in Euler's method give an underestimate R1 (dependent on A1, reference to tangents required). [2 marks]
